audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. The spectral formula for the boundary term is false; Taking real parts prevents the stated analytic continuation; Theorem 8.1 cannot provide \(H^2\) fields for every allowed \(L^2\) current
limitations: Counterevidence and alternatives: Normalizing m only inside the projector leaves the projector unchanged and cannot fix the unnormalized cross terms.
Counterevidence and alternatives: For a homogeneous local Maxwell field, C=-tau W and zero divergences, pi-W=0 gives D=tau(1-s)pi+W; local W=exp(-T*x1)(e2,e3) realizes nonzero D on the flat patch.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The local Maxwell example is not asserted to satisfy all global face conditions.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The unstretched positive-projection special case s=1 does not show the scaling error.
Counterevidence and alternatives: No PML instability or false principal weighted-L2 theorem is inferred.
Counterevidence and alternatives: E is real, so conjugation of the field cannot explain the discrepancy.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Adding an outer Re to the left still gives real residual1/50 at T=2.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Real tau and zero absorption special cases can satisfy the identity; the failure concerns complex continuation with the stated nonzero absorption.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Outer absolute values in Proposition6.3 are actually present; no finding is based on the text extraction losing them.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The counterexample is to the identity, not to the trace inequalities.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The boundary condition cannot resolve an interior Sobolev contradiction.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The source itself notes the extra H1 current regularity forced by an H2 field on p25.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The weaker L2 solution conclusion of Theorem1.15 is not contradicted.
Counterevidence and alternatives: A density argument from smooth compatible sources may repair a weaker existence statement, but all its trace and parameter properties must be proved.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Preceding(8.11) already contains the forcing and supports the correction as an omission.
Counterevidence and alternatives: Interchanging electric/magnetic block order cannot create the missing term.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The example uses smooth data, so the failure is distinct from Problem3.
Counterevidence and alternatives: This does not refute existence after the displayed correction.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The paper explicitly limits its uses of this correspondence to constant spatial coefficients.
Counterevidence and alternatives: The constant-spatial-coefficient differential substitution has holomorphic rational stretch coefficients and is valid.
Counterevidence and alternatives: This local overstatement is distinct from the real-part continuation defect of Problem2.
Limits: No independent priority survey; uniform-in-time stability and damping are explicitly open, not attributed as proved.
Limits: No claim that all complex spectral statements have been formally certified.
Limits: The complete converse after changing function spaces has not been re-proved.
Limits: External elliptic regularity, index and Fredholm results were not independently re-proved.
Limits: No complete rebuild of every Helmholtz boundary condition or estimate for the corrected form.
Limits: No counterexample to the trace inequalities themselves and no full complex-Rellich estimate repair.
Limits: Global a priori inequality not independently refuted or reconstructed.
Limits: No full compatible-density, trace or holomorphic-parameter repair; Paley-Wiener theorem not independently re-proved.
Limits: No independent full proof of the final error estimate or its external matching inputs.
Limits: No external cited paper was acquired or scientifically represented as checked in this 0407 review.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

The target is M25-0407, Laurence Halpern and Jeffrey Rauch, Stability of perfectly matched layers for Maxwell’s equations in rectangular solids, DOI 10.1002/cpa.22249 (https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.22249). The reviewed source is the undated author-hosted file `2025CPAM.pdf`, retrieved on 27 October 2026, with 72 pages [HR]. PDF and printed page numbers agree. The acquired bytes have SHA256 \[\texttt{51c36487e49c348cad99ecaf828b3a55f21}\] \[\texttt{bd9382322ee251d150c83d842cf3e}.\] The line break is typographical. The source manifest retains the uninterrupted hash. No accepted-manuscript or version-of-record label is inferred from the filename. The author listing’s issue number and the deposited journal metadata differ; that bibliographic discrepancy is outside the mathematical assessment.

Write \(W=(E,B)\) and \[A(\xi)(E,B)=(-\xi\times B,\xi\times E),\qquad
 \widetilde\partial_j=\frac{\tau}{\tau+\sigma_j(x_j)}\partial_j .\] The absorptions are nonnegative smooth functions of one coordinate, vanish on the domain of interest \(Q_I\), and have bounded derivatives of every order [Retained latex: \cite[p.~7, Assumption 1.2]{HR}]. Zero absorption is allowed. For the examples with nonzero absorption, take \[Q=(-3,3)^3,\qquad Q_I=(-1,1)^3,\] and choose a smooth bump \(b:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\), supported in \((3/2,5/2)\), equal to one near \(2\). Set \(\sigma_2=b\), \(\sigma_1=\sigma_3=0\). These coefficients satisfy all the stated absorption hypotheses. Choose the smoothing \(Q^\delta\) sufficiently close to \(Q\) that \((0,2,0)\) is an interior point and a neighborhood of \((3,2,0)\) remains a flat boundary patch. This is permitted by Definition 3.1.

For the stretched normal define, as in source Definition 3.3, \[\Pi=\prod_{j=1}^3\frac{\tau+\sigma_j}{\tau},\qquad
 \mathcal M_{ii}=\prod_{j\ne i}\frac{\tau+\sigma_j}{\tau},
 \qquad m=\mathcal M\nu,\qquad s=(m\cdot m)^{1/2}.\] For positive real \(\tau\), \(s=|m|\). For the sufficiently large complex parameters used by the source, the square root is the branch continued from positive real values. Spectral projectors \(\pi^\pm(m)\) refer to the eigenspaces of \(A(m)\) with eigenvalues \(\pm s\). Set \[P_{\mathrm{tan}}(E,B)=(\pi_{m^\perp}E,\pi_{m^\perp}B),\qquad
 C(W)=(-\widetilde{\operatorname{curl}}B,\widetilde{\operatorname{curl}}E).\] The bilinear dot product, rather than the Hermitian inner product, is used in these algebraic identities.

Recorded check: The spectral formula for the boundary term is false

Q=(-3,3)^3, QI=(-1,1)^3; smooth b supported(3/2,5/2), equal1 near2, values[0,1]; sigma2=b(x2), sigma1=sigma3=0. Qdelta retains a flat patch near(3,2,0). tau=T>0 arbitrarily large. Constant E=e2,B=e3 are H2. Proposition5.10 assumes arbitrary H2 fields and imposes no PDE or boundary condition on this test.

repair.content:
Replace tau*Ptan W in D by tau*s*Ptan W to define Ds. Then pi^±Ds=s*pi^±(tau W±C).

No complete repaired complex trace estimate is claimed.

No complete repaired theorem or density passage is claimed.

Use Uhat_k=(tau+sigma_k)^-1(fhat_k-A_k d_k W), fhat_k=c_k(-J,0).

Restrict to spatially constant coefficients for the applications actually used.
